two-sizes-sequential.why: Two loops one after the other add their costs. n and m are independent input sizes, so neither can be dropped.

two-sizes-nested.why: The inner loop runs m times for each of the n outer iterations. Calling it O(n²) would wrongly assume m = n.

halving.why: Each step halves n, so it reaches 1 after about log₂ n steps.

pointer-never-resets.why: It looks nested, but j only ever moves forward and never resets, so the while loop runs at most n times in total across all outer iterations: O(n) + O(n). This is the shape of two-pointer and sliding-window code.

doubling-outer.why: The outer loop runs about log₂ n times (i doubles), and each pass does n inner iterations.

harmonic.why: For each i the inner loop runs about n / i times. n/1 + n/2 + … + n/n = n × (1 + 1/2 + … + 1/n), and that harmonic sum grows like log n.

constant-inner.why: The inner loop always runs 1000 times regardless of n: a constant factor, which Big-O ignores.

why-drop-constants.why: n(n − 1)/2 = n²/2 − n/2. The n²/2 term dominates as n grows, and the factor 1/2 doesn't change how it grows.

faster-always.why: Big-O describes growth, not actual speed. A could have a huge constant factor, and B can be faster for small n. A wins once n is large enough.
